name: WPIL Ltd
title: WPIL Ltd - 505872 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Consolidated revenue INR501 cr (+32% YoY) and 15% EBITDA margin, but standalone domestic projects starved of Jal Jeevan funds: INR43 cr revenue and 5% standalone EBITDA margin, with INR300-350 cr receivables unpaid in Q1.

triggers.label: JJM receivables INR300-350 cr unpaid
triggers.quote: Roughly, I think, INR300 crores to INR350 crores, and we should get a majority of that.

triggers.label: Domestic project revenue INR43 cr, sector funds stuck
triggers.quote: The domestic project division remained subdued during the quarter with revenues for the quarter at INR43 crores.

triggers.label: Domestic water recovery pushed to H2
triggers.quote: We expect an improvement in the domestic water sector during the second half of the year as the sector issues are resolved.

guidance.value: 15% to 20% range; roughly 16-17% for the year
guidance.quote: overall, in the year, we find that it is in this range, roughly around 17%, I think we'll get 16%, 17%.
We believe there will be a substantial inflow this quarter.

guidance.value: PCI Africa buyout in 3 years; other subsidiaries over 2-3 years
guidance.quote: in 3 years, we will buy out the other shareholders.

red_flags.label: Standalone EBITDA margin 12.21% per call but 5% per analyst; receivables stuck in state treasuries
red_flags.quote: Only due to the project invoicing, which is very drastically lower because the sector is still facing problems, our funds are not yet released.

red_flags.label: MP government debarment from new bids
red_flags.quote: They gave us a debarment basically saying that you cannot bid for new projects until you finish the old projects.

red_flags.label: Management unable to answer segment profitability questions
red_flags.quote: We don't have the details, so I can't answer this.

red_flags.label: Unresolved litigation on terminated MP contract written back
red_flags.quote: It's a litigation that termination was in litigation. It's moved from -- arbitration, it is into arbitration right now.

evasions.topic: Project segment profitability (INR19 cr, down QoQ margin)
evasions.quote: We don't have the details, so I can't answer this.
It's not -- it's consistent with the performance of product division.
I'm sorry, I don't have that right now.
I don't know any new others.

summary.headline: WPIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% YoY to INR501 crore at a 15.04% EBITDA margin, while standalone EBITDA margin fell to 12.21% on weak domestic project billing.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR501 crore (up 32% YoY) with EBITDA of INR75 crore (15.04% margin) and PAT of INR59 crore (11.79%). International revenue rose to INR386 crore from INR197 crore, with international margin at about 15%. Standalone revenue fell 37% YoY to INR115 crore, with EBITDA of INR14 crore (12.21%) and PAT of INR6 crore, as domestic project invoicing slowed due to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) fund releases. Total order book stood at INR5,270 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR197 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit of associates and JVs
financial_highlights.change: vs about INR8 crore for full prior year, per analyst

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Revenue INR386 crore vs INR197 crore YoY; EBITDA margin improved materially to about 15%; international order book INR2,891 crore. Includes Gruppo Aturia (MENA demand), Sterling and United (Australia), WPIL Thailand, MISA Italy and PCI Africa (South Africa water contracts, 3-4 year tenure).

segments.name: Domestic product division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR72 crore vs INR65 crore YoY; order book INR459 crore. Management cited power and irrigation traction. Product order book cited as INR1,029 crore in total, split about 55% international and 45% domestic.

segments.name: Domestic project division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR43 crore, described as subdued; order book INR1,921 crore including about INR530 crore O&M. Analyst-reported segment figures showed project revenue INR260 crore and profit INR19 crore (about 7% margin), which management did not confirm. Most domestic EPC backlog is Jal Jeevan Mission, with about INR1,400 crore EPC backlog cited.

segments.name: Joint ventures
segments.commentary: Share of profit of associates and JVs INR11.24 crore; JVs are in Thailand (49% stake) and India (40% stake). Management did not split by product or project.

guidance_outlook: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margins to stay within the company's 15-20% range, with full-year margin around 16-17%.
Management expects Indian water-sector invoicing to pick up in H2 FY27, once JJM fund-flow issues are resolved; it said it had expected resolution by Q1 and now expects it in Q2.
Management expects a substantial inflow of JJM receivables (about INR300-350 crore outstanding, mostly from West Bengal) in the current quarter.
Management expects a major part of the domestic EPC backlog to execute in FY27, subject to West Bengal payment momentum.
Management intends to buy out minority shareholders over 2-3 years; PCI Africa buyout is agreed in principle within 3 years.
Management said capex for the year would be nothing substantial.
Management said MP government debarment target to resolve within about one year, with MP projects at 65-70% completion.
capex_capacity: Management said planned FY27 capex is nothing substantial.
MP government projects are 65-70% complete; target to finish within about one year, after which the debarment from new bids is expected to be lifted.
Project O&M business of about INR530 crore expected to scale as projects move into O&M next year; management said O&M margins are higher than EPC margins.
PCI Africa has begun executing large contracts won in FY26 in the South African water sector; the business was acquired in May 2025.
demand_pricing: Management said consolidated margins are stable and that most project contracts carry price variation clauses, limiting raw material exposure (mainly steel and metals) from the Middle East conflict.
International product demand: fresh MENA demand across oil and gas and water, with robust demand for gas turbine pumps.
Australian business has healthy inquiry pipelines in LNG, mining and industrial projects.
Domestic product demand: good traction in power and irrigation, with a robust inquiry pipeline.
Analyst questions on the product order book execution period went unanswered; management said product revenue is growing and will continue to do so.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East war affecting raw material prices and procurement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are stable. Steel is the main input; a short spike occurred when Middle East exports slowed, but medium- and long-term contracts balance it out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA margin fall to about 5% (analyst figure)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to very low project invoicing from JJM-related slow fund release, which is a sector-wide issue. It expects Q2 to improve and H2 to see recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How much JJM receivable is outstanding and how much was received in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR300-350 crore outstanding, mostly West Bengal and less MP. Nothing was received in Q1; management expects most of it to be disbursed this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MP government debarment and its timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: MP government issued a debarment notice citing slow project progress, barring new bids until old projects are finished. Management targets resolution within about one year; projects are 65-70% complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the MP write-back and Rutschi tax matters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one MP contract was terminated about 2.5 years ago and is now in arbitration. For Rutschi, France gave a favourable reply and the money is being claimed back; Switzerland is still pending.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR11.24 crore share of JV profit?
qa_highlights.answer: It comes from two JVs (Thailand 49%, India 40%); management said both performed well and did not split by segment.

risks_watch: Domestic project revenue remains depressed (INR43 crore) with JJM receivables of INR300-350 crore pending; the H2 recovery depends on fund release.
MP government debarment blocks new bids until old projects are completed; watch resolution progress.
Standalone margin decline and analyst-reported project profit (INR19 crore, about 7%) were not clarified by management; disclosure quality concern.
Management did not disclose total cash balance or the amount paid under the Rutschi tax matter.
Minority buyout intentions (PCI, South African and Singapore subsidiaries) are contingent on cash and contractual timing.
Quarterly consolidated revenue of about INR500 crore was flagged by an analyst as run-rate; management said it expects improvement but said outcomes depend on the volatile global situation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the international and consolidated margin story, but evasive and defensive on domestic project weakness, segment-level margins, and the MP debarment and write-back questions, often deferring details or saying data was unavailable.
key_quotes: Our consolidated margin has hit 15%, and our standard range is between 15% and 20%, so we should see it improving only further.
Most of our raw material is steel. So, we have metals and steel.
Our intention is to reduce the minority shareholding on all our subsidiaries over the, say, medium 2 to 3 years' time.
Roughly, I think, INR300 crores to INR350 crores, and we should get a majority of that.

growth.why: Management guides full-year consolidated EBITDA margin of 16-17% within a 15-20% range, backed by a INR5,270 crore order book (INR2,891 crore international, INR1,400 crore domestic EPC backlog) and expected JJM receivable inflows, but no new capacity is being added and FY27 capex is described as nothing substantial; domestic water recovery is pushed to H2 FY27.
